title: Fork of Metaphysics framework closed
description:
I’m writing to share the public release of v1.0.0 of the Metaphysics Closure Framework, now formally frozen and posted to OSF.
This work addresses a long-standing problem at the foundation of philosophy and science: how to determine, in an observer-invariant way, which metaphysical claims are admissible as knowledge claims, which must be treated as model comparisons, and which should be explicitly labeled non-operational.
What this framework does
Defines metaphysics as a model-admissibility and comparison layer, not a source of explanatory or predictive claims.
Requires all admissible metaphysical statements to be rewritten as observer-invariant model comparisons.
Enforces strict non-collapse into physics while preserving the authority of empirical science.
Terminates interpretive disputes structurally rather than rhetorically.
Demonstrates resistance to paradoxes, adversarial manipulation, and observer bias.
What it does not do
It does not claim truth.
It does not predict outcomes.
It does not introduce new entities or mechanisms.
It does not replace domain sciences.
The framework has undergone formal stress testing, live adversarial testing, observer-invariance testing, and historical/event-aligned empirical validation of the “confusion → instability amplification” limb. Based on these results, v1.0.0 is declared structurally complete and frozen. All future work will occur only as applications, empirical instantiations, tooling, or governance materials.
The OSF repository contains:
The frozen framework specification
The metaphysics–physics interface appendix
Stress-test and adversarial validation reports
A scope and limitations declaration
The formal freeze declaration (v1.0.0)
This release is intended as public infrastructure, not a manifesto. Disagreement with outcomes is expected; challenges to admissibility must be expressed as model-comparison critiques.
